findings.title: Old local recovery codes are not removed when new codes are created in user storage
findings.body: When updateCredential succeeds in the federated storage, this method only logs and never deletes any pre-existing local recovery-authn-codes credential for the user. SubjectCredentialManager.isValid checks both federated and local credentials, so codes from the previous local credential remain valid after the user regenerates recovery codes in user storage. Regeneration therefore does not revoke the old codes, contrary to the expectation that generating a new set replaces the old set.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is removed through the local-storage API
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential now prefers a federated credential, but when all its codes are used this code calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only removes a credential from Keycloak's local DB. A federated credential (whose id is owned by, and may not even be set by, the user storage) is therefore not deleted/disabled in its storage, remains configured for the user, and can leave an exhausted credential in place despite the required action being re-added; removal should go through the federated credential-disable/update path for federated credentials.

findings.title: User label and generation time are dropped when recovery codes are written to user storage
findings.body: The federated write builds UserCredentialModel solely from the credential type and the JSON list of raw codes. The supplied RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel also carries the userLabel entered on the setup form and its generatedAt/createdDate, but neither is passed to the user storage, so a federated credential cannot be returned/displayed with the label (or original creation date) that the equivalent locally stored credential has.

findings.title: Login bean still dereferences an empty Optional for users without a readable recovery credential
findings.body: The PR changes this bean to use RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which returns Optional, but immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() (and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()) with no presence check. If the federated storage returns no credential, returns one whose credentialData cannot be parsed as RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData, or all codes are used, rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException instead of handling the unconfigured/exhausted state, producing a 500 during login.
